answer: A river market stays honest when every new identity must row a distinct walnut barge across the river and carve by hand an ivory tally for every crossing, while a distinct toll-keeper stamps each tally at the far bank. The first fake owes one tally, the second two, the third six, since the nth fake owes n factorial tallies, so the tenth fake alone owes 3,628,800 tallies and five fakes owe 153. Bulk farming fails because one carver shapes one tally at a time and each barge crosses the river alone, like one ferryman rowing a single barge per tide across the wide river.
